connector: Caspian has met three Old Narnians. Today he meets dozens: bears, a squirrel, Dwarfs at a forge, a Centaur who reads the stars, and a very small Mouse with a very large bow. So many names! Group them as you go, and ask what each group wants from Caspian.

a.raw: reepicheep was very small so some creatures doubted him but his courage was the greatest of all
a.fixed: Reepicheep was very small, so some creatures doubted him, but his courage was the greatest of all.
a.why: Capital R on the name; a comma before so (cause and result) and before but (a surprise); a period ends it.

b.raw: the badger did not want armor so he kept only his claws and teeth
b.fixed: The badger did not want armor, so he kept only his claws and teeth.
b.why: Capital T starts it; a comma before so, because the second part happens because of the first; a period ends it.

s4w27cf1.h1: be·GIN is stressed on the last syllable. Double or not?
s4w27cf1.why: Double the n: begin + n + ing = beginning.

s4w27cf2.h1: VIS·it is stressed on the first syllable. Double or not?

s4w27cf3.h1: for·GET is stressed on the last syllable. Double or not?
s4w27cf3.why: Double the t: forget + t + ing = forgetting.

s4w27cf4.h1: TRAV·el is stressed on the first syllable. Double or not?
s4w27cf4.why: In American spelling, no double: travel + ed = traveled.

notes.wgrd: With a crowd of new characters, sort them into kinds (bears, Dwarfs, Centaurs, Fauns), give each kind one word, and ask what each group wants from Caspian.
vocab: A private teacher who teaches one student or a few.
Someone who takes power, like a throne, without the right to it.
The study of the stars, planets and sky.
In a strict, serious, firm way.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: port = carry, tract = pull or draw, struct = build: transport, attract, construct, instructed.
notes.grammar: But and so join two complete sentences. But says the second part goes against what you expected; so says the second part happens because of the first. Put a comma before each. Swapping but for so can flip the meaning.
notes.spelling: Suffix rules: drop the silent e (hope + ing = hoping); change y to i (empty + er = emptier); double the last consonant when the last syllable is stressed (begin + ing = beginning, but visit + ing = visiting).

why.t: The treasure chamber at Cair Paravel is still waiting for its treasures. This week Caspian learns that the old stories are true, and the Old Narnians come out of hiding one by one. Each word you build sets one more treasure in its place. This week’s Latin bases: port (carry), tract (pull) and struct (build).

wordgame.winDay: More treasures are back in their niches.
wordgame.win: More treasures are back in the chamber. port = carry, tract = pull, struct = build.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: In Chapter 6 the Old Narnians come out of hiding. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Reepicheep bows and says, “There are twelve of us, Sire,” and “I place all the resources of my people unreservedly at your Majesty’s disposal.”
items.why: He offers everything his people have, with perfect manners.

items.t: Caspian thinks Reepicheep’s whole people could fit in a washing basket. He tries hard, and successfully, not to laugh.
items.why: He will not make fun of someone who has just offered to fight for him.

items.t: The Seven Brothers of Shuddering Wood give Caspian, Trumpkin and Nikabrik mail shirts, helmets and swords.
items.why: They give their best work to the cause.

items.t: Glenstorm says, “I watch the skies, Badger, for it is mine to watch, as it is yours to remember.”
items.why: He knows his own job and does it.
items.hint: What does each creature have to do?

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. Caspian has three friends now. Today he meets a whole hidden country of them. Today’s question: how do you keep track of so many new characters, and what does each group want?
transcripts.read: So many names today! Don’t try to hold them all. Sort them as you go: the bears, the squirrel, the Dwarfs at the forge, the Centaur, the Mouse, the Fauns. Give each kind one word. And watch how Lewis starts each new visit.
transcripts.spelling: Here’s a trick for long words. Say the word and listen for the strong beat. Be-GIN. If the beat is on the last part, and it ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant: beginning. VIS-it has its beat at the front, so no double: visiting.
